The irrigation notes reference submission of as-built design plans to the City upon final inspection. The Master Comment Report identifies Austin Energy review by Rosemary Avila with reference to a Bluebeam link for AE comments, but the actual AE review comments are not accessible in the provided supplementary documents. No specific irrigation plan submission document or Austin Energy approval correspondence for irrigation is visible in the application materials provided.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.11 specifies that irrigation plan submission to Austin Energy is required 'only when irrigation system is proposed and Austin Energy coordination is required per ESPA process.' An irrigation system is clearly proposed per Sheet 31. The grouping instruction states to 'Check: Landscape plans, irrigation design, Austin Energy correspondence indicating irrigation review requirement.' While Austin Energy conducted a design review (documented in Master Comment Report), the specific comments and whether they addressed irrigation cannot be verified from the accessible documents. UCM Section 1 may require Austin Energy coordination for irrigation systems, but without access to ESPA documentation or the Bluebeam AE review comments, it cannot be determined whether Austin Energy irrigation review was specifically required or whether the irrigation plan was submitted for AE review as required. This creates an unclear status because the infrastructure exists but the documentation of AE coordination is not accessible.
findings.comment: Irrigation system is proposed but it is unclear whether the irrigation plan was submitted to Austin Energy for review as required per ESPA process. Review Austin Energy's comments via the Bluebeam link referenced in the Master Comment Report to verify irrigation plan submission and approval.

applicableAreas: electrical service routing on site plan
findings.observation: Sheet 21 is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' and depicts electrical infrastructure including transformers, pull boxes, and underground electric lines routed across the site. However, the plan contains no notes, callouts, or documentation referencing Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual requirements or UCM Section 1 compliance. The plan lacks any notation of design compliance with specific UCM standards such as clearances (UCM § 1.10.4), truck access (UCM § 1.3.16), or metering equipment installation (UCM § 1.9.3). Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains general electric notes from Austin Energy but does not address the specific UCM Section 1 routing requirements for the proposed electrical service design shown on Sheet 21. No equipment specifications, conduit sizing, or routing documentation demonstrating compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual is provided on the electrical site plan sheets.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.13 requires demonstration that 'Proposed electric service routing not shown in accordance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual' and applies to all sites. The grouping instruction states this requires 'Electrical site plan includes UCM compliance notes, clearances dimensioned per UCM § 1.10.4, equipment placement meets UCM standards, transformer locations comply with Table 1.10.4 requirements.' The preliminary electrical plan shows the general routing layout but fails to demonstrate compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual through dimensioned clearances, compliance notes, or reference to specific UCM sections. The plan is marked as preliminary, indicating it lacks the final design detail necessary to demonstrate compliance with the comprehensive requirements of UCM Section 1.
findings.comment: Proposed electrical service routing shown on Sheet 21 does not demonstrate compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1). Add UCM compliance notes, dimensioned clearances per UCM § 1.10.4, equipment specifications, and pad details to demonstrate that service routing and equipment placement meet all applicable UCM standards.

findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) documents that transmission facilities and transmission easement exist on the property through 16 separate Electric Transmission Notes. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows the proposed buildings (Buildings 1-8) and electrical infrastructure layout but does not depict or document any clearance dimensions between the proposed buildings and the existing transmission facilities. No distance measurements, clearance zones, or conflict identification are shown on the electrical site plan. Sheet 3 transmission notes require pre-construction grading coordination with Austin Energy (ET Note 2: 'Grading near electric transmission facilities must be coordinated with Austin Energy prior to commencement of grading') and mandate a safety meeting (ET Note 3). However, there is no documentation on the site plan sheets showing that clearance conflicts between the proposed buildings and transmission conductors have been identified and discussed with Austin Energy Design during the site plan phase. The coordination notes address pre-construction requirements, not design-phase conflict resolution.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.14 requires 'Clearance conflict between existing electric conductors and proposed buildings not discussed with and resolved by Austin Energy Design.' The grouping specifies checking 'Proximity of proposed buildings to electric lines; clearance dimensions; Austin Energy coordination documentation addressing conflicts.' Sheet 3 transmission notes indicate transmission facilities exist on site. Sheet 21 shows proposed buildings but without any documentation of clearance analysis or conflict resolution with transmission lines. The presence of transmission notes requiring pre-construction coordination does not constitute design-phase conflict resolution. Per UCM § 1.10.4 and the National Electric Safety Code (referenced in Sheet 3 ET Notes), clearance conflicts must be identified and resolved during design, not deferred to construction. No conflict analysis or Austin Energy Design approval letter addressing transmission clearances to proposed structures is visible in the application documents.
findings.comment: Clearance conflicts between existing transmission conductors and proposed buildings have not been discussed with and documented as resolved by Austin Energy Design. Provide clearance dimensions between all proposed buildings and transmission line conductors, and include Austin Energy Design approval documentation confirming that proposed building locations and heights comply with NESC and UCM § 1.10.4 clearance requirements.

findings.observation: The site is located in Austin, TX (3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704) within Austin Energy's service territory, as confirmed by the presence of Austin Energy Electric Notes and Electric Transmission Notes on Sheet 3 and the identification of Austin Energy as the electrical service provider in the Master Comment Report (Rosemary Avila, Austin Energy). Sheet 21 shows a proposed electrical design with transformers, meters, and underground service lines. The Master Comment Report indicates Austin Energy conducted a design review through Rosemary Avila with reference to a Bluebeam review link. However, no formal Austin Energy approval letter is present in the supplementary documents (Project Review Form, Completeness Check Results, Consolidated Site Plan Application, Master Comment Report, or Engineer's Summary Letter reviewed). No stamped electrical site plan with Austin Energy approval seal or signature is visible. The site is within 200 feet of Austin Energy components per the transmission easement notation, triggering the approval requirement.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.15 specifies 'Approval of electric system plans from Austin Energy not obtained' and applies to 'All sites requiring connection to Austin Energy system or within 200 feet of existing Austin Energy components.' The grouping instruction states to 'Check: Austin Energy approval letter, stamped electrical site plan, ESPA approval documentation.' LDC § 25-4-200 requires that 'All electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy.' While the Master Comment Report documents that Austin Energy conducted a review (with comments on Bluebeam), this does not constitute formal approval. No approval letter, stamped plan, or ESPA approval documentation appears in the accessible supplementary documents. The electrical site plan is marked as preliminary, and formal Austin Energy approval is required before the design can be finalized.
findings.comment: No Austin Energy approval letter or stamped electrical site plan with Austin Energy approval has been obtained. Submit the proposed Preliminary Electrical Design Plan to Austin Energy for formal review and approval per LDC § 25-4-200, and provide the signed approval letter and stamped electrical site plan with final application submission.

applicableAreas: electrical site plan design and specifications
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical infrastructure layout including three transformer pads, underground service lines, pull boxes, and electrical meters. However, the plan lacks all documentation required to demonstrate compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1): (1) Clearances are not dimensioned - no measurements shown from transformer pads to buildings, parking areas, sidewalks, or windows per UCM § 1.10.4; (2) Transformer pad dimensions are not specified; (3) No UCM compliance notes or callouts appear on the electrical plan; (4) No reference to Table 1.10.4 clearance requirements (10 ft hot-stick use area, 15 ft facing confined space, 20 ft from oil-filled equipment to fire escape, 5 ft from windows/doors, 12 ft from windows if lateral <5 ft); (5) No equipment specifications (kVA ratings, voltage, insulation type) are provided; (6) No truck access dimensions or bollard requirements (UCM § 1.10.4) are shown. Sheet 3 contains general Austin Energy notes but does not provide site-specific UCM compliance demonstration on the electrical plan.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.16 specifies 'Compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual not demonstrated' and applies to 'All sites requiring connection to Austin Energy system.' The grouping instruction requires 'Electrical site plan includes UCM compliance notes, clearances dimensioned per UCM § 1.10.4, equipment placement meets UCM standards, transformer locations comply with Table 1.10.4 requirements.' The preliminary electrical plan shows the general configuration but lacks the specific design detail necessary to verify compliance. Per LDC § 25-4-200, compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (adopted as part of the Utilities Criteria Manual, UCM Section 1) must be demonstrated. Without dimensioned clearances, pad specifications, and explicit UCM compliance notes, it cannot be verified that the transformer locations, conduit routing, and equipment placement meet the comprehensive requirements of UCM Section 1.
findings.comment: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan does not demonstrate compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1). Add to the electrical site plan: (1) dimensioned clearances from all transformer pads to buildings, doors, windows, parking areas, and sidewalks per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4; (2) transformer pad dimensions and specifications; (3) truck access dimensions and bollard locations if pads are within 4 feet of parking; (4) conduit sizing and routing specifications; (5) explicit UCM compliance notes confirming adherence to all applicable sections of UCM Section 1.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) visual analysis identified the presence of an 'Electrical Vault Easement' labeled near the southwest entrance of the site. The vision analysis noted this easement 'encompasses a transformer pad and pull box.' The site is located at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704 in the MF-2 zoning district, which is not part of the downtown Network Area (UCM § 1.11.5). No Network Area service is indicated on the site plans. The term 'vault easement' is used in the labeling, but the transformer within it is described as a 'pad' (pad-mounted), which typically refers to aboveground equipment. However, the use of the term 'vault' in the easement designation creates ambiguity as to whether the transformer is truly a subsurface vault installation or simply an easement area serving a pad-mounted transformer.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.22 specifies 'Vaults or meter rooms proposed outside Network Area where vaults are not permitted' and applies only when 'vaults or subsurface/enclosed transformer rooms are proposed.' UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults to the Network Area only; outside the Network Area, transformers must be pad-mounted (clear to sky) or installed in specialized niches meeting specific requirements (UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3). The site is clearly outside the Network Area. The ambiguity arises from the sheet's reference to an 'Electrical Vault Easement' while the transformer within it is labeled as a 'pad.' This terminology conflict must be clarified: if the transformer is truly installed in a subsurface vault, it violates UCM § 1.5.2.6. If it is a pad-mounted transformer within an easement area, it is compliant. The preliminary nature of the electrical plan and lack of detailed transformer installation specifications (normal pad-mounted vs. vault vs. niche configuration) prevent a definitive determination.
findings.comment: Sheet 21 references an 'Electrical Vault Easement' but the transformer within it is labeled as a 'pad.' Clarify whether the transformer is pad-mounted (compliant) or installed in a subsurface vault (non-compliant outside Network Area per UCM § 1.5.2.6). If a vault installation is proposed outside the Network Area, reconfigure to either: (a) pad-mounted transformer (clear to sky), or (b) specialized niche meeting UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3 requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls/ceilings, exterior access, proper ventilation, truck accessibility).

findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains Electric Transmission Note 6, which states: 'Warning signs must be placed under the overhead electric transmission facilities as notification of the electrical hazard.' This note addresses transmission infrastructure caution signage. Sheet 3 also contains Electric Notes 1-5 addressing Austin Energy's rights and owner responsibilities regarding electric facilities. Sheet 21 shows three transformer pad locations and underground electric lines, but the site plan does not include a construction staging plan or detailed protective signage specifications for any of the electrical facilities (transformers, pads, underground lines, pull boxes). The Master Comment Report and supplementary documents reviewed do not contain construction staging plans or site-specific caution signage details. The transmission warning signage requirement is documented in the general notes, but overall protective signage details for all existing Austin Energy facilities during construction are not shown on available plan sheets.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.24 specifies 'Caution signage not shown for existing Austin Energy facilities during construction' and applies 'Only when existing Austin Energy facilities (transformers, vaults, conductors, equipment) are present on construction site.' The grouping instruction requires 'Check: Existing utility locations, construction staging plans, protective signage details.' Existing Austin Energy facilities are present on the site (transmission easement, as noted in ET Notes on Sheet 3). While transmission warning signage is required per ET Note 6 and documented in the general notes, the site plan sheets do not show a comprehensive construction staging plan with detailed protective signage specifications for all existing electric facilities. The plans identify that caution signage is required but do not specify the locations, dimensions, or exact signage details in a construction staging plan or protective barrier plan format. This creates an unclear status: the requirement is noted, but the detailed implementation and comprehensive coverage are not documented on the available site plan sheets.
findings.comment: Transmission warning signage is required per Sheet 3 ET Note 6, but comprehensive caution signage details for all existing Austin Energy facilities during construction have not been provided. Provide a construction staging plan showing the locations of all existing Austin Energy facilities (transmission lines, transformer pads, underground lines) and specify protective barriers, caution signs, and temporary fencing required during construction per UCM § 1.10.1.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts three electrical transformer pads: one west of Building 2/northwest of Building 8 near the western property line and street entrance; one between Buildings 8 and 6 in the central driveway/alley area; and one east of Building 5 near the eastern property boundary. The vision analysis confirmed: 'There are no specific dimensions (e.g., distance lines with measurements) provided on this sheet to indicate the exact clearances from the transformer pads to the buildings, doors, or windows.' No clearance dimensions are shown from any transformer pad to: adjacent buildings (Buildings 2, 5, 6, 8), building doors or windows, parking areas, sidewalks, or fire escapes. No dimensions verify compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requirements: 10 feet minimum for hot-stick use area to adjacent building, 15 feet if facing confined space, 20 feet from oil-filled equipment to fire escape/stairs, 5 feet lateral or 12 feet vertical from windows/doors, 6 feet maximum from parking/traffic areas for truck access, or bollard locations if within 4 feet of parking.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.27 specifies 'Proposed buildings, bike racks, or site features do not meet required safety clearances from Austin Energy facilities' and applies 'Only when site is adjacent to Austin Energy facilities requiring safety clearances.' The grouping instruction requires 'Check: Site plan dimensions, Austin Energy equipment locations (transformers, vaults), clearance compliance per Table 1.10.4 (10 ft to 20 ft depending on configuration).' UCM § 1.10.4 establishes specific minimum clearances from pad-mounted transformers and distribution equipment based on configuration and adjacent features. The site has three transformer pads shown on the electrical plan with buildings, parking, and sidewalks in close proximity. Without dimensioned clearances on the site plan, it cannot be verified that any of the proposed transformer locations comply with the safety clearance requirements of UCM § 1.10.4. The preliminary nature of the design and absence of clearance documentation means compliance is unverified.
findings.comment: Transformer pad locations shown on Sheet 21 do not include dimensioned clearances to adjacent buildings, parking areas, sidewalks, or other features. Add dimensions to all transformer pads showing clearances to: adjacent buildings (minimum 10-15 feet per UCM § 1.10.4), parking/traffic areas (maximum 6 feet, with bollards if less than 4 feet), windows and doors (minimum 5-12 feet per orientation), and fire escapes/stairs (minimum 20 feet if oil-filled equipment). Verify all clearances meet Table 1.10.4 requirements.
